With the International Space Station soon being decommissioned and destroyed on re-entry, the Australian government would like to open discussions with the Japanese government in regards to the possibility of partnering up to create a new next-generation space station.

The proposed ‘Yoshida-Menzies Station’ (named after the Japanese and Australian leaders who re-established diplomatic relations after the conclusion of WWII) would initially feature the following modules (in order of launch):

  • Core Module (living quarters, power supply, guidance, communications)
  • Critical systems module (temperature control, oxygen production)
  • Docking module
  • Cargo Hold

Once these modules have been assembled, ASA and JAXA astronauts will begin to occupy and maintain the station. Following this, we will begin to add scientific modules. The launch order of these modules is yet to be determined, but will include:

  • A microgravity research module
  • A multi-purpose laboratory module
  • An EVA research module
  • A biological research module
  • An observatory module

The construction of the station will take time, but we are confident that by working together, both of our great nations are capable of making this dream into a reality.
